paper_metadata.title: Predictors of surgical outcome and pathologic considerations in focal cortical dysplasia

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, consecutive cohort from a specialized center with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and detailed baseline characteristics. The recruitment period and setting are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 166 consecutive patients who had undergone surgical treatment for refractory epilepsy and had a pathologic diagnosis of FCD at the Seoul National University Hospital between November 1995 and June 2005.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients with refractory epilepsy and FCD at a specific tertiary hospital.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: In our surgical cohort, 956 patients underwent surgical treatment for refractory epilepsy... the pathologic diagnosis of FCD was made in 206 (21.5%) patients.
items.reasoning: The study describes the total surgical cohort and how the specific FCD sub-sample was identified.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between November 1995 and June 2005.
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the recruitment period are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Seoul National University Hospital
items.reasoning: The specific institution and location are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We excluded three patients with insufficient postoperative follow-up (less than 2 years), and 10 patients with other potentially epileptogenic lesions... We also excluded 40 patients who had radiologic evidence of hippocampal sclerosis (HS) in addition to FCD
items.reasoning: Detailed exclusion criteria are provided to ensure a clean sample of FCD-only patients.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 166 consecutive patients were included.
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive patients in a surgical cohort typically implies high participation of the eligible population.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The subjects consisted of 102 men and 64 women, and the mean age of the patients at the time of surgery was 24.7 10.2 years... mean age at seizure onset was 11.5 7.0 years
items.reasoning: Table 2 and the text provide comprehensive baseline data including age, sex, seizure frequency, and history.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for all patients and explicitly excludes those with short follow-up to ensure outcome stability. The mean follow-up is long (7.94 years).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: We excluded three patients with insufficient postoperative follow-up (less than 2 years)
items.reasoning: Only 3 out of 206 potential FCD patients were excluded for follow-up reasons, indicating a very high retention rate.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (pathologic subtype) is defined using a standardized international classification system (Palmini) and assessed by pathology, which is an objective gold standard.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The diagnosis and classification of pathologic cortical dysplasia were according to the system of Palmini and colleagues: ectopically placed neurons only (mMCD), isolated architectural abnormalities (FCD 1A)...
items.reasoning: The study uses the established Palmini classification for FCD subtypes.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: pathologic diagnosis of FCD... according to the system of Palmini and colleagues
items.reasoning: Histopathology is the gold standard for FCD diagnosis; using a standardized system increases reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were divided into two subgroups: the mild pathologic group (mMCD, FCD 1A, and FCD 1B) and the severe pathologic group (FCD 2A and 2B).
items.reasoning: The grouping is based on clinical/pathological severity logic (presence of dysmorphic neurons/balloon cells) rather than arbitrary data-driven p-hacking.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The diagnosis and classification of pathologic cortical dysplasia were according to the system of Palmini and colleagues
items.reasoning: All samples were processed at the same institution using the same criteria.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Pathologically, 21 patients showed characteristics of mMCD, 89 patients of FCD 1A, 28 patients of FCD 1B, 12 patients of FCD 2A, and 16 of FCD 2B.
items.reasoning: Pathology data was available for 100% of the included 166 patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not required as there was no missing data for the primary PF.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure freedom) is a standard clinical metric in epilepsy surgery, and the study required a minimum of 2 years follow-up to ensure the outcome was stable.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcome was divided into seizure-free and not seizure-free... follow-up for more than 2 years
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined and the follow-up duration is specified.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The proportion of seizure-free patients was 56.6% (94/166) during the follow-up for more than 2 years
items.reasoning: Seizure freedom is the standard clinical outcome for epilepsy surgery.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Surgical outcome was divided into seizure-free and not seizure-free.
items.reasoning: All patients were assessed using the same binary criteria at the same institution.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study uses multivariable analysis to adjust for MRI findings and completeness of resection, other potential confounders like specific anti-epileptic drug regimens or detailed surgical techniques were not explicitly included in the model.

items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Age at operation, Age at onset, Duration of epilepsy, Men/women, Seizure frequency, Presence of 2GTCS, Presence of FC, Complete resection, MRI, EEG, PET, SPECT
items.reasoning: Many clinical and diagnostic variables were measured, but specific medication changes post-op were not detailed.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Complete resection was defined by resection of all of the MRI-visible lesions or areas of ictal onset...
items.reasoning: Key confounders like 'complete resection' are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Standard MRI was performed on either a 1.0-T or a 1.5-T unit... FDG-PET images were assessed visually and by statistical parametric mapping analysis
items.reasoning: Confounders were measured using standard clinical protocols (MRI, PET, EEG).

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients underwent brain MRI... PET was performed in 151 patients... Ictal SPECT was performed in 121 patients
items.reasoning: The protocols were consistent, although not every patient received every functional imaging test.
